correctness.rationale: With p odd prime and Q(x,y)=x²−dy², |C|=p−χ(d). For h≠0, the conic intersection equations reduce to a one-variable quadratic in the Q-orthogonal line: zero points at norm zero, one at Q(h)=4, and two exactly when χ(−dQ(h)(4−Q(h)))=1. The standard quadratic-character sum gives (p−χ(d))(p−χ(d)−2)/2 two-point shifts. Nonempty intersection sizes are 1, 2 or p±1, none divisible by p; irreducibility of the pth cyclotomic polynomial proves all their Fourier sums nonvanishing. The zero-shift conic transform is derived by additive orthogonality and Gauss squares and yields the stated Kloosterman band, with dual norm frequencies counted exactly. For two-point intersections the nonzero linear difference functional gives the complete cosine multiset. Hilbert–Schmidt-normalized Weyl diagonalization of the p^{-1}-calibrated lifting yields singular values precisely |A_g(h,ω)|, establishing rank, kernel and all multiplicities. Exact integer-residue no-zero tests, rank and full numerically evaluated spectral bands passed for p=5,7,11,13,17 of both quadratic types; separately a 625×625 direct SVD at p=5,d=1 agrees within 8e−15. The proof, not those finite checks, carries the universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Actual comparison of mathematical statements finds no identified prior conic-indicator full-orbit lifting rank AND complete singular multiset. The 2017 prime-field Gabor paper classifies orthonormal-basis windows, not a conic projector-span spectrum; Bojarovska–Flinth provides the general ambiguity/Weyl operator framework but not the arithmetic conic specialization; the 2007 sphere Fourier paper gives the zero-shift character sums without the translation-geometry and Weyl multiplicity classification. The closest 2026 hyperbolic-shell theorem was read in full and assumes dimension at least four and does not give the dimension-two split/nonsplit singular multiset; two-view conic tomography concerns a restricted linear projection operator instead. Searches and comparisons are best-knowledge evidence, not proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: The published conic two-view and extension papers were compared from available summaries, not their complete text; none claims the same operator, but a hidden implication remains possible.
A prior finite-field circle difference-set census or unindexed Gabor frame-operator calculation could implicitly contain the rank; no such complete conic singular multiplicity result was found.
The Kloosterman-valued band is an exact finite-sum description, not a closed elementary distribution of individual Kloosterman magnitudes. No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The unweighted nondegenerate quadratic conic is a canonical arithmetic Gabor window in the two-dimensional prime plane, with distinct split versus nonsplit geometries. The full lifting rank determines the number of identifiable complex matrix coordinates, and the exact Weyl kernel identifies all lost modes; the singular multiset determines finite-dimensional linear inversion conditioning and noise amplification, beyond a mere support-count exercise. The arithmetic jump between m=p−1 and m=p+1, combined with a Kloosterman zero-shift band and elementary intersection cosine bands, is a natural complete classification for every prime and both isometry types. It fills the dimension-two and nonsplit cases left by the closest higher-dimensional shell rank result, and gives the complete spectrum rather than its dimension. No downstream general theorem is asserted, and the full singular spectrum is mathematical content not implied by the generic ambiguity diagonalization alone.
